title: Provider-router routing decisions and sessionInventory operations emit one structured audit event per named interaction
description: The provider router and the sessionInventory surface (both on TAC-1204) emit exactly one structured audit event per named interaction from the `keycloak.route` and `keycloak.session_inventory` families (route decided, session listed, session revoked one, sessions revoked all-except-current, refused when unauthenticated). Every event carries fields drawn from the fixed allow-list `family` (one of `keycloak.route`, `keycloak.session_inventory`), `outcome`, `reasonClass?`, `realmSlug`, `sessionIdPrefix?`, `at`. No event may carry a token value (access token, id token, refresh token, introspection response body), a client secret, a raw claim record, or a substring of any of the above. The audit sink is the same one REQ-015 names; sink-failure posture is inherited verbatim (a sink failure logs a `keycloak.audit_sink_failed` warning event and never masks the underlying refusal).
rationale: A single cross-cutting audit REQ pointing at one TAC hides ownership when the delivery is spread across TACs. Each TAC that emits an audit family owns its own REQ so a reviewer can see the ownership at a glance and so a future author changing an audit family finds the single REQ that governs it.
